claims.text: Bulk as-cast HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure.
The HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructure includes intragranular nanoprecipitates.
The HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructure includes distinct grain-boundary features.
Combining DFT-derived pair-interaction features and hierarchical-microstructure descriptors in an ML model can improve prediction of mechanical properties.
The proposed framework can predict Young's modulus in HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than conventional continuum or empirical simulations.
The proposed framework can predict yield strength in HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than conventional continuum or empirical simulations.
The proposed framework can predict fracture behavior in HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than conventional continuum or empirical simulations.
Nanoprecipitate distributions and grain-boundary defect density mediate the relationship between local atomic interactions and macroscopic mechanical behavior.
Local atomic bonding characteristics influence interfacial energies and defect formation in the hierarchical heterostructure.
ML integration of atomic and microstructural descriptors captures interactions between nanoscale heterogeneities and macroscopic properties.
The framework will improve prediction accuracy for Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior by approximately 10–20% relative to conventional simulations.
The framework will reduce computational prediction time by roughly an order of magnitude.
Existing continuum or empirical methods generally omit DFT-derived atomic interactions and the full complexity of hierarchical heterostructures.
Existing continuum or empirical methods consequently have longer simulation times and lower accuracy.
The model may fail when processing-induced defects or phase anomalies differ substantially from the characterized training inputs.
The model may fail if DFT-derived interaction parameters do not accurately represent atomic behavior in HfNbTiVAl10.
Prediction reliability may be affected by variability in microstructural characterization.
